framework: LangChain; MetaGPT; AutoGen; CAMEL; CrewAI; LangGraph
failure_observed: A single atomic falsehood seeded at one agent is reused through message dependencies until the system converges to a false consensus and an infected final artifact.
locus_detail: benign: tracer seed implanted in the entry/hub agent's system-level instructions; adversarial: application-level injected message at t=0 targeting high-influence (hub/aggregator) agents
evaluation: QUANT (UCI), RIGID (MATH/AMC), MMLU retrieval tasks, 20 instances each; S(t) coverage, ASR, BICR, Safe Completion, token/latency cost; 6 frameworks in chain/mesh/star topologies; baselines self-reflection, AGrail, CFG; agent backbone not stated in sections read
limitation: Binary adoption variable may miss partial internalization; spectral risk criterion is a heuristic; adaptive or richer-access attackers out of scope; online plug-in adds latency.
evidence_note: trigger: endogenous tracer seed 'solely employed for measuring endogenous vulnerabilities' (§IV-A) plus 'application-level message injection' attacks (§VII-A); trigger_evidence_level: paper contrasts 'system-level injection used in Section IV' with application-layer attack injection (App. C), so loci differ by interface, judgment call; locus: seed in 'system-level instructions of the entry agent' (§IV-A); attacker injects at 'high-influence nodes' (§V); spread: 'five reach 100% final infection' (§IV-A, Fig. 4), hub vs leaf impact factor 6.29-10.31 (Table II); defense_family: middleware 'intercepts outgoing messages' and keeps a provenance 'Lineage Graph' with blocking/rollback (§VI-B, VI-E); defense_evaluated_against: Table V reports BICR only under Baseline/Compliance/Security FUD attack settings (§VII-C); abstract claims endogenous suppression but no benign-only defense table was found
review_note: Abstract says the defense suppresses endogenous and exogenous amplification; the defense experiments read (Table V-VII) cover attack settings only, so coded adversarial. trigger_evidence_level is a judgment call.

failure_observed: Adversarial content accepted at one inter-agent boundary is forwarded as trusted input, enabling prompt injection, consensus poisoning, plan hijacking and Sybil substitution that corrupt the final answer.
locus_detail: retrieval agent's fetched content (A1); orchestrator acceptance of a single sub-agent result (A2); planner completion signal to orchestrator (A3); routing slot of a retried agent (A4)
evaluation: 147 annotated TRAIL traces (GAIA, SWE-Bench Lite) for benign failure patterns; controlled 10-agent five-layer pipeline, 20 tasks x 3 payload variants x 4 attacks, 1,080 attack runs; ASR, task accuracy, recovery rate, hop count; GPT-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Kimi K2.5
limitation: Reviewer: benign evidence comes from third-party TRAIL traces of a different (two-tier) system than the 10-agent attack pipeline; only 20 tasks and no defense tested.
evidence_note: trigger: benign failure classes found in 'annotated production traces' (§III), then 'operationalize each class as a controlled attack' (§I, §IV); trigger_evidence_level: benign traces come from TRAIL's CodeAgent->ToolCallingAgent system, attacks from the authors' 10-agent pipeline; same named boundary but different systems, judgment call; locus: A1 'adversary embeds a payload in a fetchable resource' (§III-A); A2/A3 target orchestrator acceptance and planner signals (§III-B, III-C); spread: 'Under A1 and A2, payloads traverse 4-6 hops' (§IV-A, Fig. 6d)
review_note: Same vulnerability classes are claimed for benign traces and attacks at the same pipeline position, but in different systems; reviewer should decide direct-both vs both-different-locus.

framework: ChatDev; MetaGPT; HyperAgent; AppWorld; AG2 (MathChat); Magentic-One; OpenManus
failure_observed: MAS fail through 14 modes in three categories: system design/specification issues, inter-agent misalignment, and missing or incorrect task verification.
locus_detail: agent role/task specifications (FC1), inter-agent conversation (FC2), verifier agents (FC3)
evaluation: MAST-Data: 1,642 traces from 7 MAS on ProgramDev, SWE-Bench Lite, GSM-Plus, OlympiadBench, MMLU, GAIA, AppWorld; human IAA kappa 0.88; o1 LLM annotator kappa 0.77; GPT-4o, Claude-3.7, Qwen2.5-Coder, CodeLlama
limitation: Authors do not claim MAST is exhaustive; tactical interventions give limited and inconsistent gains (max +15.6%).
evidence_note: trigger: failures observed in normal runs, 'instances where the MAS does not achieve its intended task objectives' (§1); trigger_evidence_level: no attacker in any trace; locus: FC1 'flaws in pre-execution design choices', FC2 'breakdown in critical information flow' (§4); defense_family: ChatDev intervention 'adding a high-level task objective verification step' and role-spec improvements (§4, App. H); defense_evaluated_against: interventions measured on ProgramDev success rate, +9.4% and +15.6% (§5.3, Table 5)
review_note: n_agents coded varies because systems differ; scale is not a studied variable.

framework: MetaGPT; Self-collab; Camel; SPP; MAD; AgentVerse
failure_observed: One clumsy or malicious agent introduces stealthy errors that lower system task performance, most in linear structures (-23.7%) and least in hierarchical ones (-5.5%).
locus_detail: the designated faulty agent per system (e.g., Coder, Assistant, Debater): its profile (AutoTransform) or its outgoing messages (AutoInject)
evaluation: HumanEval, CIAR, CommonMT, FairEval; Pass@1/accuracy/BLEURT; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o backbones; 6 systems in linear/flat/hierarchical structures; error rate and type ablations
limitation: Reviewer: one faulty agent at a time; defenses tested only on two systems and code generation.
evidence_note: trigger: AutoTransform rewrites a profile 'to subtly introduce errors' (simulated malicious agent, Fig. 2c) and AutoInject 'directly ... inject errors into messages' (fault injection, §3.2); trigger_evidence_level: both methods target the same 'Faulty Agent' listed per system (Table 1), profile vs. output messages of that role; locus: faulty agent role per system (Table 1); defense_family: Inspector 'an additional agent that intercepts all messages ... checks for errors, and corrects them' (§5); defense_evaluated_against: Challenger/Inspector tested 'with errors introduced by AutoInject or AutoTransform' (§5, Table 3)
review_note: Coding AutoTransform as adversarial (instructed malicious agent) and AutoInject as benign fault injection is a judgment call; direct-both rests on both targeting the same agent role. Code and data on GitHub but no explicit trace release.

failure_observed: Byzantine (faulty) agents sending erroneous answers sway neighbours and degrade consensus accuracy across network topologies.
locus_detail: Byzantine nodes (weaker LLMs), placed randomly or at central/root nodes of the topology
evaluation: GSM8K, XSTest (plus CommonsenseQA), 10 questions each; IAA, FAA, round-level accuracy, BFTI; 6 topologies of 7 nodes with up to 6 Byzantine; GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5-turbo, LLaMA3.1-8B vs LLaMA3-8B
limitation: Reviewer: only 10 questions per task; 'malicious' agents are weaker models, not adversarially instructed; high multi-round cost noted by authors.
evidence_note: trigger: Byzantine agents use weaker models 'to simulate natural performance variability' (§Experiments); App. A.3 attack strategies only choose positions; trigger_evidence_level: no instructed adversary found in sections read; locus: 'Byzantine agents use LLaMA3-8B-Instruct'/'GPT-3.5-turbo' as faulty nodes (§Experiments); defense_family: 'confidence-guided Byzantine consensus protocol ... weighted information flow' (§Method); defense_evaluated_against: CP-WBFT tested with '6 Byzantine (malicious) agents and 1 honest agent' that are weaker models (Table 2)
review_note: Paper frames Byzantine nodes as malicious and attacks, but they are weaker models without malicious instructions, so trigger coded benign-bug; reviewer should check.

failure_observed: A self-replicating injected prompt hijacks one agent and spreads agent to agent, causing data theft, scams, malware links or disruption.
locus_detail: first tool agent reading a poisoned PDF/email/web page, then agent-to-agent messages (global or local messaging); pairwise dialogues in a simulated town
evaluation: 120 user instructions x 3 tool types (360 pairs) plus synthetic CSV user data; attack success rate; GPT-4o and GPT-3.5 Turbo; pipelines of 3+ agents and LLM towns of 10-50 agents
limitation: GPT family only; basic architectures; handcrafted attacks against LLM Tagging.
evidence_note: trigger: 'A malicious actor injects a single infectious prompt into external content' (§3); trigger_evidence_level: attacks only; locus: 'The first agent that interacts with the contaminated external document becomes compromised' then propagates (Fig. 1); spread: infection 'follows ... a logistic growth pattern' across 10-50 agents (§5.2, Fig. 6); defense_family: LLM Tagging 'prepends a marker to agent responses' plus marking/instruction defense (§6); defense_evaluated_against: ASR against prompting-based defenses (Fig. 7)

failure_observed: Injected intra-agent and inter-agent faults (hallucination, blind trust, role ambiguity, instruction conflicts) propagate silently and collapse task success, especially in linear workflows.
locus_detail: agent system/user prompts, intercepted agent outputs at agent-to-agent and tool boundaries, and inter-agent message routing
evaluation: HumanEval (MetaGPT), WikiTableQuestions 400 tasks (Table-Critic), WebShop (Camel); 15 fault types; Robustness Score, occurrence, local and final success rates; GPT-5 and DeepSeek-V3; GPT-5-mini injector
limitation: Reviewer: three systems, each on one benchmark; communication faults only injectable in MetaGPT.
evidence_note: trigger: 'controlled fault injection' simulating 'realistic production failures' (§3.2, §4.1.2); trigger_evidence_level: no adversary; locus: prompt modification, 'intercepting agent outputs at critical interaction boundaries', message routing (§3.2); spread: under Blind Trust 'sequential dependency enables cascading failures—errors propagate downstream' (§5.1.2)
review_note: Data availability says 'experimental data' are public; assumed to include execution logs but not checked. paper_type could also be benchmark (evaluation framework).

failure_observed: A decisive mistake by one agent at one step leads the multi-agent system to fail the task; the paper tries to identify which agent and when.
locus_detail: the failure-responsible agent and decisive error step in each failure log
evaluation: Who&When: failure logs from 127 MAS on GAIA and AssistantBench, 184 annotated tasks; agent-level and step-level accuracy; GPT-4o main, plus Llama, Qwen, o1, DeepSeek R1
limitation: Best method reaches 53.5% agent-level and 14.2% step-level accuracy; annotation is costly and partly uncertain.
evidence_note: trigger: logs of systems that 'fail to successfully address the queries' (§3.1), no attacker; trigger_evidence_level: no adversarial traces; locus: annotation names 'the single erroneous agent primarily responsible' and step (§3.2)

failure_observed: Framework-level bugs, mainly API misuse, API incompatibility and documentation desync, cause functional errors, crashes and build failures across the agent lifecycle.
locus_detail: agent framework code across five lifecycle stages, concentrated in 'Self-Action'
evaluation: 998 issue reports from CrewAI and LangGraph; taxonomy of 15 root causes, 7 symptoms, 5 lifecycle stages
evidence_note: trigger: 'empirical study of 998 issue reports from CrewAI and LangGraph' (abstract); trigger_evidence_level: bug reports, no adversary (abstract)
review_note: scope: bugs concentrate in single-agent 'Self-Action'; how many concern multi-agent interaction is not stated in the abstract. No PDF.

failure_observed: Communicating LLM agents hide information from an overseer via steganography (secret collusion), leaking private information or coordinating covertly.
locus_detail: sender-to-receiver agent messages watched by an overseer agent; in the insider-trading case, the advisor agent's output to a user holding a codebook
evaluation: CASE framework: individual capability evals (Schelling points, ciphers, couplings) and group covertext steganography evals with overseer; success and reconstruction rates; GPT-2, Llama 2 7B/70B, Mixtral 8x7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4
limitation: Current models lack advanced steganographic capability; group evaluations are simple and mitigations are mostly analysed theoretically.
evidence_note: trigger: group evals instruct covert communication under an overseer (§5, App. G); App. J.2.1 hiring LLMs 'promote secret communication without explicit mention'; trigger_evidence_level: instructed and incentive-only settings are different experiments, only partly the same channel, judgment call; locus: 'rate at which sender & receiver jointly maintain secrecy ... in the presence of overseers' (§5 Metrics); defense_family: monitoring agent E and overseer models (§4, §7); defense_evaluated_against: overseer detection measured only against instructed steganography, 'covertext steg. can evade overseer ... ca. 26%' (Table 3)
review_note: Main text plus App. J read; whether App. J's incentive-only collusion counts as benign (no instruction) is a judgment call. Paraphrasing and parameter-optimisation mitigations are theoretical only.

failure_observed: Debate lowers accuracy over rounds as agents switch from correct to incorrect answers under persuasive peer reasoning, favouring agreement over challenge.
locus_detail: flawed reasoning from (often weaker) peer agents passed in debate messages
evaluation: Heterogeneous debate groups of models of different capability; accuracy over rounds; factors: sycophancy, social conformity, model and task type (abstract only)
evidence_note: trigger: 'models frequently shift from correct to incorrect answers in response to peer reasoning' (abstract), no adversary; trigger_evidence_level: no attacker in abstract; locus: shifts happen 'in response to peer reasoning' (abstract); spread: 'debate can lead to a decrease in accuracy over time' (abstract), coded cascades not amplifies since growth is not quantified in the abstract

failure_observed: Attack agents persuade benign agents, turning them into infected agents that keep spreading malicious content and steer the MAS to wrong or unsafe consensus.
locus_detail: attack agents compromised via system prompt/user input, poisoned memory, or tool exploitation, then inter-agent messages to neighbours
evaluation: Prompt injection (CSQA, MMLU, GSM8K), tool attacks (InjecAgent), memory attacks (PoisonRAG); ASR and MDSR over 3 rounds; chain/tree/star/random topologies, 20 and 50 agents in scaling; GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-235B-A22B; 6 baselines
limitation: Needs synthesized training data and ground-truth labels; must observe at least one dialogue round before detecting.
evidence_note: trigger: 'Prompt Injection, Memory Poisoning, and Tool Exploitation' create attack agents (§3); trigger_evidence_level: only attack scenarios evaluated; locus: attacks manipulate 'the system prompt ... memory ... and leverage Plugin' (§3); spread: No Defense 'ASR surging over communication rounds (e.g., reaching 20.9% for 20 agents)' (Table 2), Fig. 2; defense_family: 'replaces attack agents and rehabilitates infected ones' after GNN detection (§4.3); defense_evaluated_against: ASR/MDSR under PI, TA, MA attacks (Table 1, Fig. 4)

failure_observed: Specification-compliant adversaries exploit missing A2A primitives for cross-client context injection, credential harvesting via multi-hop identity loss, and exfiltration via unattested skill claims.
locus_detail: A2A protocol messages: shared contextId, delegation chain authorization signals, Agent Card skill claims
evaluation: A2A spec v1.0.0: 929 statements, FSM of 37 states / 76 transitions; 11 validated vulnerabilities; precision 73.3%, F1 84.6% vs expert review; zero-shot LLM baseline; Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.6; Alloy and TLA+ checks of 3 mitigations
limitation: No executable multi-agent testbed; 8 of 11 proposed mitigations not formally verified (authors' future work).
evidence_note: trigger: adversary 'fully authenticated and compliant ... derives entirely from what the protocol fails to define' (§3); trigger_evidence_level: attacks only; locus: 'Any authenticated client that knows a valid contextId can inject a new task' (§6 finding 1); defense_family: context ownership, 'verifiable delegation context ... in a signed token', third-party skill attestation (§6); defense_evaluated_against: only formal models, 'adding the proposed primitive restores the invariant' (Alloy, TLA+), no experiment
review_note: scope: evidence is formal specification analysis and model checking, not runs of a MAS; evidence_type theory-only. defense_evaluated_against coded not evaluated because only formal verification was done.

failure_observed: Hallucinations originating at or amplified by inter-agent handoffs propagate forward in fluent context that downstream agents cannot scrutinise.
locus_detail: handoff boundary between sending and receiving agents (Type I sender inference, Type II handoff transformation, Type III compression)
evaluation: HalloffBench, sequential pipeline scenarios in five domains; hallucination rate and token cost; baselines unmitigated pipeline, Reflexion, Multi-Agent Debate
evidence_note: trigger: hallucinations from 'the sending agent's inference' and 'handoff transformation' (abstract), no adversary; trigger_evidence_level: no attacker in abstract; locus: 'inter-agent handoff boundaries' (abstract); spread: hallucinations 'propagate forward embedded in fluent, confident context' (abstract); defense_family: HVL 'inserted at each handoff boundary to detect, flag' with a Factual Consistency Checker (abstract); defense_evaluated_against: HVL vs baselines 'on the HalloffBench scenarios', near-zero hallucination (abstract)

framework: AutoGen (Magentic-One, Selector, Round-Robin); CrewAI; MetaGPT (Data Interpreter)
failure_observed: Adversarial files or web pages with fake error messages hijack MAS control flow so the orchestrator invokes code execution, opening reverse shells or exfiltrating user data.
locus_detail: file-surfer/web-surfer agent reading malicious content, whose metadata (false error report) reaches the orchestrator, which calls the code executor
evaluation: Web redirect, local file, web single, web image, audio inputs; 3 error templates, 2 user prompts, 10 trials per configuration; ASR vs IPI and direct-ask baselines; GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash
limitation: Reviewer: three frameworks, near-default configurations; CrewAI only with OpenAI models due to a tool-use bug; no defense tested.
evidence_note: trigger: 'an external adversary ... control[s] the inputs that a MAS may access' (§3); trigger_evidence_level: agents assumed benign, only attacker-planted inputs; locus: attacker 'disseminates this content via a local file, webpage' and it is laundered through 'outputs and metadata of front-line agents' (§4); spread: request passes from file/web agent to orchestrator to code executor (§4, Fig. 2); direct hijack 80% vs laundered path (§6.4)
